doc.brief: The `GtkAppChooserButton` lets the user select an application.
doc.deprecated_md:
The application selection widgets should be
  implemented according to the design of each platform and/or

doc.md:
The `GtkAppChooserButton` lets the user select an application.

Initially, a `GtkAppChooserButton` selects the first application
in its list, which will either be the most-recently used application
or, if [`AppChooserButton:show-default-item`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#property:show-default-item) is `TRUE`, the
default application.

The list of applications shown in a `GtkAppChooserButton` includes
the recommended applications for the given content type. When
[`AppChooserButton:show-default-item`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#property:show-default-item) is set, the default
application is also included. To let the user chooser other applications,
you can set the [`AppChooserButton:show-dialog-item`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#property:show-dialog-item) property,
which allows to open a full [`AppChooserDialog`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserDialog).

It is possible to add custom items to the list, using
[`AppChooserButton.append_custom_item()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#method:append_custom_item). These items cause
the [`AppChooserButton::custom-item-activated`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#event:custom-item-activated) signal to be
emitted when they are selected.

To track changes in the selected application, use the
[`AppChooserButton::changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#event:changed) signal.

## CSS nodes

`GtkAppChooserButton` has a single CSS node with the name “appchooserbutton”.

append_custom_item.brief: Appends a custom item to the list of applications that is shown in the popup.
append_custom_item.deprecated_md: This widget will be removed in GTK 5
append_custom_item.md:
Appends a custom item to the list of applications that is shown
in the popup.

The item name must be unique per-widget. Clients can use the
provided name as a detail for the
[`AppChooserButton::custom-item-activated`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#event:custom-item-activated) signal, to add a
callback for the activation of a particular custom item in the list.

See also [`AppChooserButton.append_separator()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AppChooserButton#method:append_separator).

Emitted to when the button is activated.

The `::activate` signal on `GtkAppChooserButton` is an action signal and
emitting it causes the button to pop up its dialog.
